Cashly Launch QA Report

25 November 2026 · Cashly POS + ERP · Revision 33c8fdf

Launch decisionCoverageBug reportRetests and false alarmsSuggestionsRemaining launch checksEvidence

Launch decision

Hold public launch. The core cash register, offline queue, HQ enrollment, procurement and sample accounting flows worked. Restaurant and delivery testing found duplicate kitchen orders, premature readiness and inconsistent COD records. Smart Analytics and cross-time-zone closing also need correction before those workflows are sold as ready.

194scenario executions, including retests
10confirmed findings
92 / 92existing backend tests passed
Passedproduction frontend build

Tests ran on the production build in Edge with .NET 10 and an isolated PostgreSQL 18 database. A second database ran the enrolled outlet. Fictional businesses, staff, sales and taxpayer records were used. Desktop page walks and 390 px mobile checks covered rendering. Browser actions and database assertions covered the transaction workflows listed below.

Frontend lint reported 111 errors and 10 warnings. This is a code-quality gate. Each customer-facing finding below has separate functional evidence.

Bug report

Critical findings affect order or payment integrity. High findings block a major workflow or regional rollout. Medium findings affect a specific action or integration input.

Critical QA-01 · Browser + PostgreSQL

Retrying a waiter order can create duplicate tickets

How to reproduce
Add one item to a table order on the waiter tablet. Interrupt only the first server acknowledgement after it accepts the order. Press Fire to Kitchen again after the failure message.
Observed
Cashly displayed “Failed to send order to kitchen” even though the first order was saved. One cart became two unpaid orders and two kitchen tickets.
Impact
Kitchen staff can prepare the same meal twice and the counter can see two charges for one request.
Fix and acceptance test
Give each tablet submission a durable order ID and reuse it on retry. Confirm the existing order if the server already saved it. Repeat the lost-response test and verify one order and one ticket.

pos-frontend/src/pages/OrderTab.tsx:103–141 and Pos.Api/Program.cs:7536–7542

Critical QA-02 · Delivery + accounting

Delivered COD shows paid with no recorded cash receipt

How to reproduce
Create an unpaid cash delivery, mark it ready, assign a fixture rider, and select Mark Delivered & Paid. Fetch the saved order.
Observed
The saved delivery was Completed with IsPaid=true, amount paid PKR 0, paid date empty, and order total PKR 232.
Impact
Payment totals and the day used for reports can disagree with the actual cash collection.
Fix and acceptance test
Record amount, tender and paid timestamp through the same payment service used for counter settlement. Keep rider-held funds separate from counted drawer cash until reconciliation. Replay the delivery confirmation and verify one posting.

Pos.Api/Program.cs:8511–8534 and 10794–10814

High QA-03 · Kitchen + dispatch

A multi-station order is ready before all stations finish

How to reproduce
Send a single unpaid order with one Grill item and one MainKitchen item. Mark only the Grill ticket Ready.
Observed
The entire order moved to ReadyForDispatch while the MainKitchen ticket was still pending.
Impact
A counter or dispatcher can release an incomplete order and trigger a premature ready notice.
Fix and acceptance test
Compute order readiness across all station tickets or require an expediter confirmation. Validate dispatch transitions on the server. Test one, two and three stations.

Pos.Api/Program.cs:8437–8473

High QA-04 · New business + delivery

A new business cannot create riders from its delivery setup

How to reproduce
Register a business and open its Delivery board. Look for rider setup. Submit the rider creation operation against the application API in the test business.
Observed
The project exposes a rider list but has no rider creation action. A normal rider create request returned HTTP 405. Delivery testing had to use a rider inserted in the disposable database.
Impact
A new outlet can reach Ready for Dispatch and have nobody available to assign.
Fix and acceptance test
Add a branch-scoped rider setup form and create, edit and deactivate actions. Test an empty business from first rider setup through dispatch.

Pos.Api/Program.cs:8537–8544 and pos-frontend/src/pages/DeliveryBoard.tsx:66–69

High QA-05 · Delivery + COD closing

Rider settlement reuses already settled and in-flight orders

How to reproduce
Complete one PKR 232 cash delivery and settle with exactly PKR 232. Refresh pending COD. Then assign a second order that is still in transit.
Observed
Settlement saved with zero variance. The same PKR 232 remained outstanding. The in-transit order also entered the pending amount.
Impact
A manager can overstate cash expected from a rider or reconcile the same delivery twice.
Fix and acceptance test
Settle a fixed set of completed, unpaid-to-HQ deliveries once. Store the order-to-settlement relationships and have the server calculate the expected amount. Verify the outstanding total falls as settlements close.

Pos.Api/Program.cs:8544–8582 and pos-frontend/src/pages/DeliveryBoard.tsx:116–159

High QA-06 · Closing report + time zones

End-of-day report defaults to the browser date

How to reproduce
Open a Pakistan branch’s Z-report from a browser set to America/Los_Angeles during the time when the branch has reached the next day.
Observed
The screen selected 2026-11-24. The same branch’s server business day was 2026-11-25.
Impact
A remote manager can read or print the wrong day and interpret an apparent shortage or missing sales incorrectly.
Fix and acceptance test
Use the server-resolved location business day for the initial date and show the branch time zone on screens and prints. Add midnight and DST coverage where supported.

pos-frontend/src/pages/ReportsManagement.tsx:66 and Pos.Api/Program.cs:10794–10804

High QA-07 · Reports + UI/API contract

Smart Analytics crashes on a successful response

How to reproduce
Sign in as the Enterprise restaurant owner after entering test orders. Open Smart Analytics.
Observed
The API returned HTTP 200. The browser fell into the error boundary with “Cannot read properties of undefined (reading toLocaleString).” The UI expects summary.avgOrderValue and an array of predictions. The API sends avgOrderValue at the top level and a single prediction number.
Impact
The analytics screen becomes unavailable even for an entitled user with sales data.
Fix and acceptance test
Share a typed response schema and use contract tests for empty, populated and gated states. Check that range buttons change the corresponding calculations.

pos-frontend/src/pages/SmartAnalytics.tsx:21–35, 215, 291 and Pos.Api/Program.cs:15863–15884

High for international rollout QA-08 · Localization + catalog

USD business displays PKR in its catalogue

How to reproduce
Register a United States business, verify its USD register context, create a 12.50 item, and open Product Catalog.
Observed
The USD configuration and amount persisted. The catalogue UI still described its prices in PKR.
Impact
Staff can interpret an item amount in the wrong currency. The catalogue currency proof leaves reports and exports requiring the same check.
Fix and acceptance test
Use the configured currency code and formatter in product forms, receipts, reports and exports. Verify decimal and zero-decimal currencies against roundtrip totals.

pos-frontend/src/pages/MenuManagement.tsx:599–600

Medium QA-09 · Register + print

Unpaid bill Print button has no action

How to reproduce
Add an item to the POS cart and click the enabled Print the bill button. Observe the preview and browser print call.
Observed
No preview opened and no print call was made. The paid receipt’s Print Receipt button invoked printing in a separate passing test.
Impact
Staff cannot print a bill for review before taking payment.
Fix and acceptance test
Connect the button to an unpaid bill preview and printer path, or present a clear unavailable state until it is supported.

pos-frontend/src/pages/PosTerminal.tsx:1232–1240

Medium QA-10 · Inventory API + data entry

Date-only stock expiry can return a server error

How to reproduce
For a grocery or pharmacy SKU, receive a valid future batch through the inventory API using a calendar date such as 2099-01-01.
Observed
The API returned HTTP 500. PostgreSQL rejected an Unspecified DateTime for its timestamp-with-time-zone column. The browser Stock In form converted its expiry value and saved a batch successfully.
Impact
Direct imports or connectors that submit calendar dates can get a generic failure instead of usable validation.
Fix and acceptance test
Represent expiry as a calendar date consistently or normalize accepted inputs before persistence. Validate bad input with a specific 400 response.

Pos.Api/Program.cs:10178–10228 and pos-frontend/src/pages/InventoryManagement.tsx:212

Retests and false alarms

  • HTTP 200 returned only the signed-in company’s products. Known product IDs from both businesses were used in the retest.
  • Retried separately. Manager login, counter activation and tablet activation passed. Initial transport timeouts do not establish a product bug.
  • The settlement reply is a receipt summary. Reading the saved order and table confirmed that the order was paid and the table released.
  • The API intentionally returned HTTP 402 with an upgrade message and feature code for Starter inventory.
  • The enum used for a percentage promotion is Percent. The corrected request saved and applied the discount.
  • Corrected tests used pickupToken, quoted an upgrade instead of the current plan, and signed into 2-step verification using the registered email. The corrected workflows passed.
  • The original browser selectors expected different labels. The actual waiter order and authorized platform pages passed on retest.
  • The early browser selectors waited for a heading the retail view doesn’t use. The later check confirmed the actual PKR copy in the USD catalogue.
  • Browser Stock In saved a valid future expiry. The isolated API’s date-only input error is still tracked in QA-10.

Suggestions for launch

  1. Fix order integrity first. Add duplicate protection on every order entry point, a final kitchen readiness rule, a branch rider directory and one settlement per completed COD order. Toast’s prep-station and expediter flow is a useful benchmark. Toast prep-station workflow
  2. Add a guided close of day. Show unpaid checks, rider collections, pending offline sales and drawer variances together. Require a counted float, actual cash and a reason where a manager approves a variance. Square close of day · Shopify register sessions
  3. Expose each queued offline sale. Show its local receipt, till, age, and sync or rejection status. Give managers a resolution path before they clear browser data or close a location. Square pending offline payments
  4. Keep register actions attributable. Keep a named user, branch and register on every refund, void, discount and cash movement. Add manager approval regression tests wherever the business permits overrides. Shopify staff roles and register attribution
  5. Use one supported rollout at a time. After fixes, run one café and one retail location through a real opening, mixed orders, closing and next-morning check. Expand to head-office outlets, then international configurations after their own checks pass. Shopify rollout guidance

Remaining launch checks

  • Complete real payment and refund authorization, provider settlement and reversal using the launch provider’s sandbox. The run verified locally recorded card tender, tax and a plan quote.
  • Exercise fiscal submissions and receipt acceptance in each enabled authority’s sandbox. Check printing, barcode scanners, cash drawers, kitchen printers and order tablets on the models intended for launch.
  • Run the Windows installer and upgrade on clean target machines, a production-like backup schedule and restore drill, and a representative peak-hour load test. The isolated PostgreSQL dump and restore were exercised here.
  • Expand the browser suite across the remaining form fields, plan conversions and add-ons, iOS Safari and Android hardware. Finish email delivery, password reset, WhatsApp, third-party delivery adapters and notification failure/retry with their test environments.
  • Verify long outages, overnight shifts, collapsed or replaced tills, and multiple outlets closing at once. Validate currency, rounding, dates and reports for each launch market.
